hero.title: Disk-backed images and compiled Wasm.
hero.lede: The gateway keeps retained images in temporary files instead of heap buffers. The broker maps verified compiled providers from disk, and chat connections recover within a finite retry budget.

summary: Retain images without keeping their bulk bytes on the heap, and reuse compiled providers across compatible broker starts. Neither change moves permission out of the broker.

metrics.label: compiled-hash check per artifact per startup

highlights.title: Images live in a bounded disk cache.
highlights.body: The gateway keeps one copy of retained image bytes in private temporary files. Generated PNGs receive scoped IDs you can reuse in later edits. When the cache reclaims an image, model history gets a release notice instead of stale bytes.
points: sessions.assetRetentionBytes sets the budget; zero disables assets
Unavailable edit inputs fail without refetching or substituting an image
Use disk-backed scratch; decode and upload buffers still use memory

highlights.title: Compatible starts reuse compiled Wasm files.
highlights.body: The first start compiles each managed provider and stores a hash-addressed artifact. Later starts verify the compiled bytes once and memory-map the file. Each invocation still gets a fresh Wasm sandbox with its existing limits.
points: compileOnLoad: true bypasses all compiled-cache reads and writes
A missing index compiles once; corruption fails startup
Stop every user of a mapped artifact before clearing the cache

highlights.title: Connection recovery has a finite budget.
highlights.body: Chat adapters start concurrently and share bounded backoff rules. Healthy connections keep serving while another reconnects. If one adapter exhausts its budget, the gateway drains and exits nonzero for its supervisor to restart.
points: Repeated flapping spends the same finite recovery budget
Monitor recovery and exit events, not only gateway_started
Connection recovery never replays outbound effects

path.title: The broker verifies before it maps.
path.body: A compatible cache avoids compilation, not verification. The provider store must stay trusted and immutable while its compiled files are mapped.
path.ariaLabel: A compatible cached provider loading into the broker

changes.title: Traces report observed memory growth and fuel use.
changes.body: Provider calls report the largest observed individual linear memory alongside fuel consumed when a final reading exists. Startup spans separate compilation cost from cache verification and mapping. These values are not process RAM or a heap profile.

changes.title: Related media can enter one session.
changes.body: WhatsApp collects media-first bursts for three seconds by default; debounceMs: 0 keeps immediate admission. Telegram collects native media groups in a fixed three-second window. Each receipt keeps its trace, linked to the shared execution.

changes.title: Check scratch mounts and remove compileCachePath.
changes.body: An old tmpfs mount still consumes RAM even when image bytes leave the heap. Use disk-backed gateway scratch with room for the retention budget and temporary IO. Remove the retired compileCachePath field, and allow the provider store to write compiled artifacts on a cache miss.

detailsIntro: The new traces help you compare startup and invocation costs. Check your deployment’s storage before expecting either disk-backed change to help.

telemetry.title: authority moved to the gateway or model
telemetry.body: The model still asks and the separate broker still authorizes. Cache files and retained images grant no permission to call a provider.
telemetry.note: A compromised gateway can vouch for any subject in its attestor lane. This release does not harden that boundary.

packages.name: Homebrew
packages.body: The generated formula installs both executables from the attested release archives.

packages.name: crates.io
packages.body: Every public crate is published at the application version. Downstream builds do not inherit the workspace-only tracing-core patch used by the release archives and image.

packages.name: Container
packages.body: The Debian 13 distroless image carries both executables from the release archives and the pinned provider components.

installIntro: Install both daemons from the attested archives, or use one of the packages below. The Helm chart has its own publication schedule.

scopeIntro: Xavier runs Dekopon on a Raspberry Pi. That deployment is not a hardened multi-tenant service, and this release makes no measured production memory-saving claim.
